transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in, or what's been on your mind lately?

Well, I guess I'm here because I just can't seem to stop starting things. It's like... I launch all these projects all at once. Work plans for my team, schedules for new IT certifications, completely overhauling my home network, sending out messages to old contacts I haven't spoken to in years. It just gets so intense. I blow right past normal limits, working all hours, until my wife or my director at work has to actually step in and tell me to stop.

Do these intense bursts of starting many projects come and go in distinct stretches—lasting days to weeks—that feel different from your usual self, or is this basically how you've always been for as long as you can remember?

Yeah, they definitely come and go in stretches. It's not how I always am. It's more like... for a few weeks at a time, I'll feel almost electric, just completely unstoppable. But during those same weeks, if there's even a tiny delay with something I'm working on, or if my wife just asks a simple question about what I'm doing, I can really snap at her. It just feels like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose.

Have you ever gone through a separate stretch of time—days or weeks—where you felt persistently down, low on energy, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy, that was different from these energetic periods?

Yeah, I do get those too. It's pretty much the exact opposite of those energetic weeks. 

There are these stretches where I'll wake up just feeling... I don't know, like a failed version of myself. Everything just feels really heavy and flat. When it gets like that, I don't care about the projects or the network upgrades at all. Honestly, even just answering my wife's normal, everyday questions feels like it's just too much effort. So, yeah, I definitely have those low periods.

During those energetic, unstoppable weeks, has it ever gotten so extreme that it caused serious problems—like nearly losing your job, major conflicts, reckless spending, or needing to be hospitalized?

Yeah, it has. It definitely causes problems. At work, I was actually put on leave recently because a huge network migration I pushed through completely failed. I just moved way too fast. 

And at home... well, my wife has had to step in a lot. She has to stop me from spending too much on new equipment, or tell me to go to bed when I'm still working at 3 AM. And like I said, those conversations usually turn into arguments. 

It's also messed up other parts of my life. I used to be really involved in church music, I went rock climbing, and I mentored some junior IT guys. But I've pulled away from all of that because I just can't reliably show up or follow through on anything when I'm bouncing between these extremes.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports distinct, days-to-weeks-long periods of elevated, expansive/irritable mood with increased goal-directed activity (multiple simultaneous projects), decreased need for sleep, excessive involvement in activities with painful consequences (reckless spending, work project failure requiring leave, marital conflict), and irritability when interrupted—meeting criteria for a manic episode with clear functional impairment. These episodes alternate with distinct periods of depressed mood, anhedonia, low energy, and psychomotor/motivational slowing lasting days to weeks, meeting criteria for major depressive episodes. The cyclical, episodic nature with clear symptom-free baseline distinguishes this from a personality-based or persistent mood disorder (ruling out F34.0/cyclothymia given severity) and the presence of depressive episodes with a history of full mania supports Bipolar I Disorder (F31) over unipolar mania (F30) or depression alone.
